info.name: Egoola API — Seller (admin)
info.description:
The admin side of sellers: seller management (create, edit, documents, delete), the Seller Request queue (cursor pagination, filters, ordering), review, approve / reject, and the profile change history. Read docs/seller-verification-guide.md alongside it. The seller-facing APIs (sign-up, seller login, own profile, resubmit) are in Egoola-SellerApp.postman_collection.json.

Run top to bottom. The [Setup] requests (a seller signs up) need a real JPG / PNG / WEBP / PDF chosen in the Postman app.

request.description: Public endpoint — no token needed. Returns access + refresh JWTs carrying actor_type=admin. Every Seller Management endpoint below is Admin-only.
Exchanges the saved refresh token (14-day life) for a new access token (1-hour life). Run this instead of logging in again once the access token expires.

Public — no token. Multipart form. The seller is created unverified and inactive and joins the admin's Seller Request queue. **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

exec: pm.test("password and tokens are not returned", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('password'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('access'); });

item.name: [Setup] Seller signs up — with business profile (public)

request.description: Same endpoint with the optional parts: more documents (`media_for` + `media_file` pairs, same order), a profile photo, and the business profile as a JSON string in `info` (every business field is required when `info` is sent). **Pick a JPG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file for each `media_file` row in the Postman app** — a shared collection can't carry file paths, so under Newman these file rows are empty and the request fails with 400.

exec: pm.test("still unverified and inactive", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('unverified'); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); });

request.description: The admin's Seller Request queue: only self-registered sellers nobody has acted on yet. **Cursor pagination** — the response has `next` / `previous` links and no `count`. Newest first by default.

exec: pm.test("cursor response shape", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('next'); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('previous'); pm.expect(b.results).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('count'); });

pm.test("both registrations are in the queue", () => { const ids = pm.response.json().results.map(r => String(r.id)); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('request_seller_id')); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('full_seller_id')); });
pm.test("every row is a request", () => { pm.response.json().results.forEach(r => pm.expect(r.is_seller_request).to.eql(true)); });
pm.test("newest first", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; for (let i = 1; i < r.length; i++) pm.expect(new Date(r[i-1].created_at) >= new Date(r[i].created_at)).to.eql(true); });

request.description: `ordering` takes `created_at`, `name` or `id`, with a leading `-` to reverse.

exec: pm.test("oldest first", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; for (let i = 1; i < r.length; i++) pm.expect(new Date(r[i-1].created_at) <= new Date(r[i].created_at)).to.eql(true); });

request.description: `limit` sets the page size (default 20, max 100). The `next` link carries an opaque `cursor`; the next request below follows it.

exec: pm.test("one row and a next link", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.results.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(b.next).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test("no previous link on the first page", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().previous).to.eql(null); });

item.name: List requests — follow the next link

request.description: Paste nothing — the previous request saved the full `next` URL in `request_next`. Use the URL exactly as given.

exec: pm.test("a different row", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.results.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(String(b.results[0].id)).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('page1_id')); });

request.description: Filters: `status`, `verification_status` (also `__in=a,b`), `creator_type`, `country`, `state`, `city`, `thana`, `email_verified`, `phone_verified`, `has_business_profile`, `business_type`, `created_from`, `created_to`, `search` (name, email, phone), `ordering`, `limit`.

exec: pm.test("both registrations match", () => { const ids = pm.response.json().results.map(r => String(r.id)); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('request_seller_id')); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('full_seller_id')); });

item.name: List requests — only those with a business profile

exec: pm.test("only the full registration", () => { const ids = pm.response.json().results.map(r => String(r.id)); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('full_seller_id')); pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('request_seller_id')); });

item.name: Waiting requests — count for a menu badge

request.description: The queue has no `count` (cursor pagination). The normal Seller list does, and accepts `is_seller_request=true`, so use it for a "Seller Request (n)" badge.

item.name: Retrieve a request — documents and history

request.description: The detail page the reviewer works from: `media` holds the uploaded documents (`media_for`, `media_url`), `business_info`, addresses, and `verification_logs` (the first entry is the registration itself).

exec: pm.test("NID uploaded", () => { const m = pm.response.json().media; pm.expect(m.length).to.be.at.least(1); pm.expect(m.map(x => x.media_for)).to.include('nid'); m.forEach(x => pm.expect(x.media_url).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty); });

pm.test("registration is in the history", () => { const l = pm.response.json().verification_logs; pm.expect(l[l.length - 1].creator_type).to.eql('seller'); pm.expect(l[l.length - 1].verification_status).to.eql('unverified'); });

item.name: List requests — by the date they joined the queue

request.description: `requested_at` is the sign-up time, and is set again every time a rejected seller resubmits. The queue's default order is `-requested_at` (newest request first). Also `requested_from` / `requested_to` (YYYY-MM-DD).

exec: pm.test("newest request first", () => { const r = pm.response.json().results; for (let i = 1; i < r.length; i++) pm.expect(new Date(r[i-1].requested_at) >= new Date(r[i].requested_at)).to.eql(true); });

item.name: Edit an address — stays in the queue

request.description: Only an action on `verification_status` or `status` takes a seller out of the queue. Other edits leave it there.

item.name: Admin edits the seller — logged with the admin's name

request.description: Admin edits go to the same log. Status and verification changes do not (they are in `verification_logs`).

exec: pm.test("newest log row is by the admin", () => { const l = pm.response.json().profile_change_logs[0]; pm.expect(l.creator_type).to.eql('admin'); pm.expect(l.changed_fields).to.eql(['present_address']); pm.expect(l.new_data.present_address).to.eql('Admin corrected address'); });

item.name: Admin reads the seller — profile change log

request.description: `profile_change_logs` (newest first) is on the seller **detail** only. One row per save that changed something, by the seller or by an admin. `changed_fields` names the keys; `previous_data` and `new_data` have the same keys with the value before and after. Documents appear as a `documents` list, the business profile as `business_info` (only the changed parts), a password change as `"[hidden]"`. `creator_type` says who made the change: `seller` or `admin`. Status and verification changes are in `verification_logs`, not here.

exec: pm.test("newest row: address change by the admin", () => { const l = pm.response.json().profile_change_logs[0]; pm.expect(l.creator_type).to.eql('admin'); pm.expect(l.changed_fields).to.eql(['present_address']); pm.expect(l.previous_data.present_address).to.eql('New address, Feni'); pm.expect(l.new_data.present_address).to.eql('Admin corrected address'); });

request.description: Approving takes two fields: `verification_status` (the KYC decision) and `status` (lets the seller log in). Send both in one request. Either one leaving its old value clears `is_seller_request`.

item.name: Approved seller is out of the queue

exec: pm.test("approved one is gone, the other waits", () => { const ids = pm.response.json().results.map(r => String(r.id)); pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('request_seller_id')); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('full_seller_id')); });

request.description: `inactive` pauses a seller: they can still log in and edit their profile, but nothing else, until an admin sets `active` again. This is separate from `verification_status` (an approved seller stays verified).

exec: pm.test("inactive, still verified", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('inactive'); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('verified'); });

request.description: A rejection always needs a note. The failed request changes nothing — the seller stays in the queue.

exec: pm.test("rejected and out of the queue", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_status).to.eql('rejected'); pm.expect(b.is_seller_request).to.eql(false); });
pm.test("history has the registration and the rejection", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().verification_logs.length).to.eql(2); });

item.name: The flag cannot be set by a client

request.description: `is_seller_request` is read-only: only registration sets it and only an admin action on the status clears it.
A suspended seller cannot log in and their token stops working at once.

item.name: Seller management (create, edit, documents, verification, delete)

request.description: Admin-only. List rows use SellerListSerializer — no media/business_info/verification_logs, those only appear on Retrieve.

Minimal create. Because the actor creating this row is an Admin, verification_status defaults to "verified" and verification_note defaults to null — you don't need to send either. A future public self-registration flow would default to "unverified" instead; you can still override the default explicitly by sending verification_status yourself (see "Create Seller — explicit verification_status" below).

item.name: Seller Login (for the permission-boundary test below)

request.description: A Seller's own login — returns a token with actor_type=seller. Must run right here, straight after "Create Seller" and before "Update Seller — Change Password" further down — seller_login_email/seller_login_password default to the exact credentials "Create Seller" just registered, and they go stale the moment the password-change request runs. Its only purpose is populating {{seller_token}} for "Seller actor forbidden from Sellers management" near the end of this folder. A seller logs in with phone number + password.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Dhaka Gadget House",
  "email": "dhaka.gadget@example.com",
  "phone": "+8801711000222",
  "password": "Sell@12345",
  "info": {
    "business_type": "Retail",
    "main_product": "Mobile phones & accessories",
    "owner_name": "Dhaka Gadget House",
    "employees_range": "1-10",
    "annual_revenue": "< $50,000",
    "established_year": "2022"
  }
}

request.description: `info` is the seller's 1:1 business profile, created in the same call. It comes back read-only as `business_info` on this and every later response for this seller (Retrieve, Update). In a multipart request (e.g. alongside profile_pic or media files) send `info` as a JSON-encoded string instead of a nested object — multipart has no nested-object syntax.
An Admin can override the verified-by-default behavior at create time by sending verification_status explicitly — whatever you send here is honored as-is.

item.name: Create Seller — rejected with no note (expect 400)

request.description: verification_note is mandatory whenever verification_status is "rejected" — on create just as much as on update. Expect a 400 with a verification_note error.

Includes `business_info` (the validated SellerInfo row, or null), `media[]`, and `verification_logs[]` — the full verification-status change history for this seller, newest first. `verification_logs` only appears here, never on List.

exec: pm.test('detail has history and media lists', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.verification_logs).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(b.media).to.be.an('array'); });

request.description: Any subset of fields. This example only touches `name` — verification_status/verification_note/verification_logs are all left completely untouched, and no verification log entry is written, because verification_status isn't part of this request.
Hashed server-side before saving. The seller can log in with the new password immediately (POST /api/v1/auth/seller/login/); the old password stops working.

item.name: Update Seller — Upload Media & Profile Picture

formdata.description: nid | birth_certificate | certificate | gallery_image | gallery_video | other
Paired with the media_for above by position (1st media_for <-> 1st media_file, etc.).
Optional, repeatable — ids of existing media rows to remove. Leave out if you're only adding files.

request.description:
multipart/form-data — Postman sets the Content-Type boundary automatically, don't add it by hand. Add as many media_for/media_file pairs as you have files; they're matched by position, so provide exactly one media_for per media_file, in the same order. There's no in-place edit of an existing file: to replace one, delete its id via media_delete_ids and upload a new one in the same call.

The file fields (`profile_pic`, `media_file`) have no file selected — file paths aren't portable between machines, so this collection can't ship one. Click each file field in Postman and select a real image/document from your own disk before sending; run as-is (e.g. via Newman/CI) it correctly fails with 400 ("file load error: missing file source"), not a bug.
Same rule as on create: rejecting without verification_note in this same request is a 400, even if the seller already has a note stored from a previous rejection.
Sets verification_status to rejected and stores the note — both on the seller row (verification_status/verification_note) and as a brand-new entry appended to verification_logs.

exec: pm.test('note stored', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().verification_note).to.eql('Trade license document is unreadable, please re-upload.'));

item.name: Update Seller — Re-verify (note clears to null)

request.description: Run this right after "Reject (with note)" above. verification_note is NOT sent here, so it is stored as null on the seller row and in the new log entry — the old rejection note does not carry over. If you want a note to still be visible after this change, you must resend it yourself in this same request.

exec: pm.test('note cleared to null, not carried over', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().verification_note).to.be.null);

item.name: Seller actor forbidden from Sellers management (expect 403)

request.description: Runs while the seller is still active (before the suspend step below). Needs "Seller Login (for the permission-boundary test below)" (earlier in this same folder) to have already populated {{seller_token}}. Every endpoint in this collection is Admin-only (IsAdminActor) — a valid Seller token still gets 403, not 401, since the token itself is valid, just for the wrong actor type.

This request doesn't include verification_status at all, so verification_status/verification_note/verification_logs all come back exactly as they were — no new log entry is written. Confirms verification bookkeeping only reacts to an actual verification_status change, not to every update.

item.name: Suspended seller's earlier token is rejected (expect 401)

request.description: The seller was just suspended above. Their access token is still validly signed and unexpired, but the account is re-checked on every request (apps/authentication/backends.py), so it now gets 401 instead of the 403 an active seller gets.
Cascades — deletes the seller's media, business_info, and verification_logs rows along with it.
Cleanup for "Create Seller — with Business Info", so this collection can be run again.
Cleanup for "Create Seller — explicit verification_status (Pending)", so this collection can be run again.

exec: // A fresh value for every request, so emails and phones never repeat (the built-in {{$timestamp}} only changes once a second).
